rootAssessment: Using the cadastral codigo as identity failed on one bounded viewport: two original map records (OBJECTID_1 44608 and 45458) have different polygon parts with non-overlapping interiors and a shared boundary under the same code. A separate native-record audit passed all bounded viewport, three-row paging, fresh exact-ID, absence, footprint and binding checks for 259 unique OBJECTID_1 records. All 259 geometries are valid, but a different pair (45091 and 44584) overlaps by 0.334 m² in independent metric GEOS QA. Runtime remains held for cadastral component identity and source-topology review, with no source repair or feature exclusion. Public access/reuse notices remain scope information.

rootCompletePartsFollowThrough.reason: The native codigo contract now passes all bounded runtime checks with complete native parts: 259 source records assemble 258 cadastral parcels, including two touching records for one code. No identifier substitution or shape repair is needed. Independent GEOS still finds a 0.3338069837 m² triangular overlap between two different parcel codes; its minimum rotated rectangle has sides about 0.934 m and 0.715 m. This is a source-boundary conflict, not a thin floating-point edge. Runtime remains held until a faithful ground interpretation can handle it; no source parcel was excluded, clipped or moved.
